parsed.summary: The rounding change in applyDiscount() is correct and Checkout is covered by passing tests for the 105-cent/10% case and the zero-discount case. Order Import is affected by the same change but no passing test exercises it with a discount, so the Order Import claim is unverified.

findings.title: No passing test exercises Order Import rounding for the REQ-17 case
findings.detail: REQ-17 lists Order Import as an affected workflow. importOrder() calls applyDiscount() at src/import/orderImport.ts:28, so its totals change. The only Order Import test (tests/orderImport.test.ts:5) passes a malformed row and expects a column-count error, so it fails in parseOrderRow() before applyDiscount() is called. The test map lists applyDiscount() for it, but that test never reaches the discount maths. No passing test shows that a row like 'A-1,105,10' gives 94 cents, or that 'A-1,105,0' stays at 105. REVIEW.md items 3 and 4 require this evidence, and a passing suite does not stand in for it. The author's claim that Order Import 'gets the same rounding' rests only on reading the code.
findings.suggestedCheck: Add and run an importOrder test for 'A-1,105,10' expecting totalCents 94, and one for 'A-1,105,0' expecting 105.

findings.title: Caller claim 'no callers other than Checkout and Order Import' is not established
findings.detail: The code index lists only checkoutTotal() and importOrder() as callers of applyDiscount(). It does not show dynamic or cross-module use. The ledger test posts a 94-cent charge, but postCharge() is not shown to depend on applyDiscount(). Any other consumer of discounted totals would change silently, and the evidence does not rule that out. Item 2 of REVIEW.md asks for every caller, including those the diff does not touch.
findings.suggestedCheck: Run a repository-wide search for applyDiscount and for imports of src/pricing/discount.ts, and confirm whether postCharge() or anything in src/payments takes a discounted total.
